root_cause.text: The rxrpc ACK parser relied on `skb_condense()` to flatten fragmented skbuffs into a contiguous buffer, but `skb_condense()` can silently fail to consolidate the data, causing subsequent direct pointer access to `skb->data` to read from non-contiguous memory regions in fragmented UDP packets.
root_cause.evidence: The patch explicitly states "AF_RXRPC assumes that it can just call skb_condense() and then validly access the SACK table from skb->data and that it will be a flat buffer - but skb_condense() can silently fail to do anything under some circumstances." The fix replaces the unsafe direct pointer access (`u8 *acks = skb->data + offset`) with a safe `skb_copy_bits()` call that explicitly extracts the SACK table into a pre-allocated local buffer (`u8 sack[256]`), eliminating the dependency on `skb_condense()` succeeding and preventing out-of-bounds reads from fragmented packets.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix potential out-of-bounds memory access in SACK processing by safely copying ACK data into a bounded buffer and validating the copy operation before use.
intent_record.what: Refactored the SACK (Selective Acknowledgment) table extraction logic by: (1) introducing a local 256-byte buffer `sack` with alignment, (2) replacing direct pointer arithmetic into skb data with `skb_copy_bits()` to safely copy the ACK data, (3) adding bounds checking via `umin()` to limit nsack to 256, (4) replacing the modulo-based index reset logic (i == 256 check with acks -= i and i = 0) with a conditional reset every 256 iterations (i & 255 == 0), and (5) adding detailed comments explaining SACK table format.
intent_record.how: The change improves safety by copying ACK data into a kernel stack buffer before processing rather than directly dereferencing skb data, which prevents potential out-of-bounds reads. The `skb_copy_bits()` call validates the copy operation and returns an error if the data is unavailable, allowing early return. The loop logic is simplified: instead of resetting the index and pointer when i reaches 256, it now resets the pointer every 256 iterations using bitwise AND, which is clearer and avoids potential integer wraparound issues.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove conditional skb_condense() call from ack processing to simplify code logic.
intent_record.what: Removed a conditional block that called skb_condense(skb) when nr_acks > 0, eliminating 3 lines of code (the if statement and its body).
intent_record.how: This change removes a socket buffer memory optimization that was conditionally triggered when processing acknowledgments with one or more ack records. Without this call, the skb will no longer be compacted/consolidated in memory after processing acks, potentially using more memory but simplifying the code path.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit completely rewrites the rxrpc ACK and data handling code. The vulnerability root cause was that the old code relied on `skb_condense()` to flatten fragmented skbuffs before direct pointer access to `skb->data`. In this rewritten version, the code explicitly avoids the problematic pattern. Key evidence: (1) The commit message states 'We avoid calling skb_clone(), pskb_pull() and pskb_trim()' and 'keep track of the offset and length of the content of each packet in the sk_buff metadata'; (2) In the new `rxrpc_input_ack()` function, ACK parsing uses `skb_copy_bits(skb, sp->offset, &buf.ack, sizeof(buf.ack))` instead of direct pointer access - this safely copies data from potentially non-contiguous buffers; (3) In `rxrpc_input_data()`, the code uses `skb_copy_bits(skb, offset, &flags, 1)` for jumbo packet validation instead of assuming contiguous memory; (4) The `rxrpc_extract_header()` function no longer calls `pskb_pull()` and instead sets `sp->offset = sizeof(whdr)` to track position; (5) All packet parsing now uses offset-based `skb_copy_bits()` calls which safely handle fragmented skbuffs without requiring consolidation. The fix is complete and comprehensive - the vulnerable construct (relying on `skb_condense()` followed by direct pointer access) is entirely absent from this rewritten code.
